name: maboss
title: Showcase: viva-maboss — MaBoSS stochastic Boolean networks as a pluggable engine
description: viva-maboss bridges MaBoSS (via the compiled cmaboss backend) into process-bigraph as a process that advances a continuous-time Boolean network interval by interval, re-sampling the joint state and emitting per-node Boolean state and ensemble on-probability. This showcase proves the engine on a minimal two-node toggle network — the Boolean layer that plugs into multiscale composites (e.g. Boolean cell-fate coupled to kinetics and a spatial field).
question: Does viva-maboss expose the MaBoSS engine (cmaboss) as a process-bigraph process that advances a stochastic Boolean network one coupling interval at a time and emits ensemble on-probabilities — the Boolean layer for multiscale composites?
hypothesis: Wrapping MaBoSS as a process-bigraph process and running a two-node network (A activated by B, B repressed by A) should produce bounded, non-degenerate ensemble on-probabilities for both nodes that settle around 0.5 — the signature of the network's limit cycle — using the real cmaboss stochastic simulator.

executive.what_is_this: A demonstration that the MaBoSS stochastic Boolean-network simulator can be driven as a plug-in engine inside process-bigraph. It runs a tiny two-gene regulatory network and reports, interval by interval, the probability that each gene is ON across a stochastic ensemble.
executive.verdict: The toggle composite runs cmaboss end to end: both nodes' ensemble on-probabilities stay bounded in (0,1) and settle near 0.5 (A ~ 0.53, B ~ 0.52) over the run — the acceptance band met in a clean-venv run of the pinned engine.
executive.verdict_detail: Study toggle-switch: over a 30-interval run, the last-10-interval mean on-probabilities are A = 0.529 and B = 0.520, both inside [0.3, 0.7]; neither node locks to 0 or 1 (observed on viva-maboss 0.1.3 / cmaboss 1.0.0b34, 2026-11-27). The A=B / B=!A logic makes this a 4-state limit cycle, so the bounded ~0.5 marginals are its signature — not bistability.

scientific_argument.main_claim: MaBoSS can be exposed as a reusable process-bigraph process that advances a stochastic Boolean network and emits real ensemble statistics, ready to be the Boolean layer of a multiscale composite.
evidence_for: Both nodes' ensemble on-probabilities remain bounded and non-degenerate and settle near 0.5, exactly as the network's 4-state cycle predicts.
The run is seed-reproducible and emits per-interval Boolean states alongside the marginals, so the process genuinely advances the cmaboss ensemble.
evidence_against: This is a toy two-node network chosen to exercise the bridge; it demonstrates the engine, not a biologically calibrated regulatory model.
caveats: The network's marginals reflect a limit cycle; an "anti-correlation" or bistability reading would be wrong for this specific logic.
